title: Cast your cares (1 Peter 5:1–11)
hook: clothe yourselves with humility; the adversary prowls; God cares for you
tomorrow: is faith the finish line, or only the first step?

segments.voice: Hospitality without grumbling: a welcome without the sigh, gifts held as a steward. Love covers. The guests go home, and the house goes quiet, and then the worrying starts.

Two in the morning, the night before something big. The worry won't sit still. You set it down; it climbs right back on. So how do you throw a worry that won't let go of you? 1 Peter answers with a throwing word: "Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you." Not set it down politely. Cast it. And the line doesn't stand alone. It sits between a set of clothes and a lion.
screen: `TWO IN THE MORNING.` → `IT CLIMBS BACK ON.` → `CAST IT.`

segments.voice: First, the clothes: "be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble." Humility, here, is something you put on. Then the line in full: "Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you." Look at the reason it gives. It isn't a technique for calming down. It's a claim about God: he cares for you. That's why the throw can land somewhere. The line sounds like a psalm: "Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee." Then, right after, the lion: "Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour." Handing over a care isn't falling asleep. You stay awake, just lighter. And if the worry climbs back on? Nothing in the line says you only get one throw. Then the chapter's promise for afterward: "after that ye have suffered a while," God will "make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you." A while. Not forever. So for a sleepless night this week: you don't have to win the argument with the worry. You can throw it, again if you need to, toward someone who cares.
screen: `CLOTHED WITH HUMILITY.` · `CAST IT: HE CARETH FOR YOU.` · `BE SOBER, BE VIGILANT.` · `A WHILE, NOT FOREVER.` · then, large: `HE CARES FOR YOU.`

segments.voice: Write one care on a scrap of paper, a few plain words. Fold it, set it down out of reach, and leave your hand open on your knee for the sit. If a care ever feels too heavy to carry alone, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.
Cast your cares. First Peter, chapter five: throw the weight on God, because he cares for you, and stay awake.
Your line: he cares for you. That's the reason the throw can land. Sleep well tonight.

fork.setup: your friend has her driving test tomorrow and has rehearsed every way it could go wrong, twice. she texts at midnight. what does 1 Peter 5:7 offer her?
